    Differential expression with moderated t-statistics

    Source: R/bio-omics.R
    bio_diff_expr.Rd

    Compares two groups feature by feature (genes, transcripts, proteins or metabolites) using the empirical Bayes moderated t-test of Smyth (2004), the method behind limma, written in base R. A one-way linear model is fitted to every feature, the residual variances are shrunk towards a common prior estimated from all features, and moderated t-statistics with extra degrees of freedom are formed for the chosen contrast. P-values are adjusted with the Benjamini-Hochberg method.

    Usage

    bio_diff_expr(
  .data,
  feature,
  sample,
  value,
  group,
  treatment = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  transform = c("none", "log2", "log2_cpm"),
  robust_prior = TRUE
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame in long format.

    feature, sample, value, group

    <tidy-select> Columns identifying the feature, the sample, the measured value and the experimental group of each sample.

    treatment, reference

    Levels of group to compare (log fold change is treatment - reference). By default the first level is the reference and the second the treatment.

    transform

    "none" (values are already on a log scale), "log2" (adds 1 then takes log2) or "log2_cpm" (counts to log2 counts per million with a prior count of 0.5).

    robust_prior

    If FALSE, use ordinary t-tests (no variance moderation) instead.

    Value

    A <bio_omics> sorted by p-value, with columns feature, log2fc, ave_expr, t, p_value, p_adj and std_error. The prior degrees of freedom and variance are kept as metadata; see glance().

    Details

    The input is tidy (long) data with one row per feature and sample. Counts can be transformed to log2 counts per million first.

    References

    Smyth, G. K. (2004). Linear models and empirical Bayes methods for assessing differential expression in microarray experiments. Statistical Applications in Genetics and Molecular Biology, 3, 3. doi:10.2202/1544-6115.1027

    Benjamini, Y. and Hochberg, Y. (1995). Controlling the false discovery rate: a practical and powerful approach to multiple testing. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society B, 57, 289-300. doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x

    Examples

    de <- bio_diff_expr(expression_sim, gene, sample, count, condition,
  treatment = "stress", reference = "control", transform = "log2_cpm"
)
de
